[spoiler=Election 2027 Results; New Government Will Be Inaugurated Next Month]

[b]National Electoral Commission of Baladullah[/b]

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم 

With a voter turnout of 72%, the results are in for the elections held on 12 October 2027:

Sultan: Hassan ibn Nasser al-Badawi (66%)

Wazir: Hussein Zuhraini (57%)

Prime Minister: Moshe ben Haktiva (40%, other candidates had 37% and 23%)

The elections proceeded safely, freely, and openly, with the only instances of disturbances being some agitators in Maghlaba who were harassing pro-government election monitors, and who were promptly arrested. 

In shaa Allah, the next period of 2027-2032 will be one of a deepening and strengthening of the Islamic socialist revolution, Divine Law system, and increased authority and autonomy for smaller bodies of political and economic power.

Minister Portfolio for 2027-2032:

1. Abdoul Mahonomayi will be retained as Foreign Minister

2. Musa al-Yahudiyyah will be retained as Defense Minister

3. Asiya bint Ghulam al-Tariqi will replace Maryam al-Khalidi as Minister of Religious Affairs 

4. Abdullah al-Hassani will be appointed Minister of Virtue (overseeing the Ministry of Enjoining Good and Forbidding  Evil, which was previously part of the Interior Ministry)

5. Khadijah al-Maghreba will be retained as Minister of Trade

6. Parvez Shahshamanshi will be appointed as Minister of Interior

7. Yahya an-Nasarai will be appointed as Minister of Technology and Research

8. Ismail Duruzi will be appointed as Minister of Industry (which will also absorb the Ministries of Finance and Economy)

9. Khalid al-Asad will be appointed Minister of Health

10. Hossein al-Rashidi will be appointed Minister of Agriculture

11. Safia bint Mahmoud al-Turabi will be appointed Minister of Education

12. Others are pending at the moment

Priorities for 2027-2032:

-Upgrade, strengthen, and improve the military, including the application of current technologies to all fields, increasing drone and missiles production by at least 75%, investment of 20 billion dirhams into military research and production, and training exercises every two months for all branches of the armed forces

-Applying Shariah Law of the time of Prophet (peace be upon him) and the righteous caliphs in all spheres

-Decentralization of various political and economic institutions and encouragement of mass participation in all political and economic bodies (Neighborhood Councils, Village Councils, Town Councils, Workers and Farmers Councils, etc)

-Investing heavily in anti-racism education and programs to improve the conditions of minority communities, especially the Omori

-Continue to improve the sustainability of economic growth and environmental protections in all spheres

-Reduce bureaucracy and inefficient state and government practices through consolidation of various organizations and ministries whenever possible

-Accelerate the anti-corruption campaign in all spheres, especially the highest levels of government and economic power 

-Improve protections for whistleblowers and protections for watchdog organizations, especially in the economic and religious sectors
[/spoiler]

[b]Trouble in the East: June 15th - October 2nd, 2027[/b]

[i]Six months ago, a dangerous underground criminal was found dead on an APD officers front step. Six months ago, we found out that he was alive. There are two official state death certificates. His name was Yuri Kabalev, member of the Kabalev family, affiliated with the Sasanov Syndicate. We made 19 more arrests with the help of Mr. Anton Luschek and several other informants. And yet we havent scratched the surface of this problem, Governor.[/i]

Just 2 hours before, APD Chief Clem Kiedrowicz had requested a meeting with the Dniezhidnov Governor, several Governors Office Ministers, and officers from surrounding departments. After Six months of work unearthing criminal rings in Andrudin, gathering a case for her department, and connecting the Greater Andrudin Area, she barged into the Governors office and refused to leave. 
[i]Weve found too many bodies over this, already.[/i] She continued, [i]We need direct communication with the KVNA, but we should involve the GTNO and BDEP. This is a nationwide issue.[/i]
The Governor cleared his throat, [i]Youre asking a lot of me on little notice. I can bring it to the House, but its up to the other Governors from there. But youve been very persuasive, Ms. Kiedrowicz, and I look forward to working more with you on this front.[/i]

The next convening of the House of Governors was a tense one. It was a joint session with the House of Commons and the Royal Cabinet. They spent six hours on a few points: Concerns raised by the Dniezhidnov Governor, a budgeting bill, and a couple of minor points that should have gone over smoothly. This wasnt even close to the case.
Immediately, after the Dniezhidnov Governor had said his piece, several PRF representatives hijacked the conversation, making sweeping generalizations about ridiculous welfare programs, and handouts to certain populations. After several attempts by not only the Governors, but the Queen herself to redirect, the session was called to recess. While both houses left the chamber, Queen Elena and her Cabinet remained at their seats.
[i]Unbelievable.[/i] she started, holding her head in her hands.
[i]Sorry excuse for a governing body. We pay those guys?[/i] Red said over a chuckle,
[i]This cant be allowed to stand. When we resume, Ill call back the Governors and let the House of Commons know theyre no longer required.[/i] Elena sighed.
[i]Just like that?[/i], replied Susana,
[i]Just like that. The continuance of such an ineffective body is a disservice to the nation. We can do better.[/i]
She stood from her chair and left the chamber. Both Houses were waiting in the outer lounge, accompanied by guards, executive assistants, Press, and Palace servants. Elena entered and cleared her throat while another dispatch of guards entered behind her.
[i]The behavior here today has been unacceptable and will not stand-[/i] she began, glaring around the room. [i]Am I meant to believe that previous Commons sessions have been conducted in the manner I saw in that chamber? Petty, insignificant grudges that you hold stand staunchly in the way of real, meaningful progress. If I allow this to continue my job becomes an impossibility.[/i] She turns to the guards behind her, [i]Please escort the former members of the HoC off campus- Civilians arent allowed this close to the Chamber without a press pass.[/i]
Instantly, the dismissed House members stood and began either shouting or begging in protest.
Look at the meeting notes!, and This isnt fair! erupted from the group as they were escorted from the palace. Press attempted through a swarm of guards to get answers from the Queen herself, coming away with small statements akin to Its not tyranny on the horizon, were about to replace the Commons with a far better, more effective body. Its unfortunate to take such executive action, but in our governments infancy hard choices must be made for the greater good.

| [u]BREAKING[/u] | [b]2028 Election[/b]: AB!'s Got Talent has a winner

[sub]Erene RP[/sub]]
[i]DEUMIBLA - Advance, Banhockia!'s Headquarters[/i]

Following another quiet week in the relatively calm election season, a phenomenon analysts supposed would be different, the nation begins to gear up for the day, coming in three months' time. Though, a reason that the race has, so far, been quite peaceful is due to the uncertainty of the country's second-major party, [i]Advance, Banhockia![/i] (AB!) in their quest to find a good fit for their presidential candidate.

The pretext to this situation is that former opposition party, and main political and social rival of AB!, the CGT, had found itself in a weird position, one it never faced: the incumbency was theirs. The first time in their history. President Lernei Sammite led the coalition to a position of power, in which it also controversially, though indirectly, assisted fellow Horizonists to enter the upper chamber, the Senior Directory, so as to strengthen its already dominant position in the lower chamber. Either way, Lernei's government has found obstacles throughout its five years of governance, though the CGT still sees him performing well in the polls. What they had not been anticipating, though, is AB!'s steady rise in the same.

The CGT has been building a much stronger position in the executive than it has in the image of its legislators, seen in what has been revealed by aggregator BHE365, based outside of the country. Currently, what it has registered demonstrates that the CGT's overall numbers are not very stable, and that they've mostly remained in a range around the mid-thirties. In the meantime, Advance, Banhockia! has been advancing slowly, and is now about neck-and-neck with the governing party. And, with the most recent announcement, it is expected that what has so far been a lowly tide may become a massive wave.

A happening similarly noted when Union 45, an also-rising force, decided upon Ambuer Mehelsaa as their representative, AB! has internally selected Garnei Lazayev as their presidential candidate for the 2028 general elections. Garnei was not born in Banhockia, rather in Sikirsk, but has lived in the Antipodean nation for 29 years. Having moved to Banhockia in 1995, later returning to his homeland for business reasons and once again coming back, seeking to implement key concepts of more modernized economies such as that of Sikirsk, Garnei served as a top officer at vehicle manufacturer Mavar. In the future, he'd collaborate with Galliumco, helping expand its services and having a part in its investment in local infrastructure. By 2007, he'd cemented himself in the Banhock business scene, though he mostly kept a low profile. Being one of the richest men in the country, he decided to move to Ermanban island (specifically the Basala estate/subdivision) and fund rare earth mining operations near the coastline. Even with putting these factors into consideration, he simply appeared on a few lists of the wealthiest of his new countrymen, though, because of the 'perceived low value' of his lands, he managed to keep most of his riches and even earned some more with the fruits of his investments.

He maintained this standing for years, until his wife, Lara Lazayev, entered politics as an estate politician who campaigned for the liberalization of building regulations. Garnei himself impulsed her efforts, and offered to pay the subdivision 𝔽'120 million ($2.1 million), a considerable part of his fortune, which by now was mostly in real value. He intended to control territory in Ermanban's southwestern coast, an empty area with presumedly unexploited fresh water reserves, with prices rising in anticipation of a rough winter. The businessman found some success, eventually reinvesting into the estate and also contributing to the budget stabilization of the island's university. This time, though, in a furious political sphere which had just experienced a fund-disclosure scandal during Habel Samaba's tenure, it was inevitable that his lobbying would become a nationwide story.

Though, he gained notoriety as a shrewd investor who'd managed to escape from the limelight. While said characteristic partially led to what occurred, as his little fame allowed such inconspicuous conduct, Garnei then became a symbol of what many Banhocks aspired to, an almost invisible public face, yet an otherwise important and competent impact on the society. When it was fully understood to what extent his support of [i]Advance, Banhockia![/i] was Lara typically allied herself with people affiliated to the Verticists Garnei was immediately installed a frontrunner for the upcoming elections, at least as a parliamentarian. Though, before Habel Samaba had even warned AB! that she would not run in the election, Garnei dispelled rumours of his own candidacy. Rather, his wife rose to prominence and was elected to Basala's only elaboratorship (seat), however in the very disillusioning 2023 ballot which saw her party lose half of their representation.

Garnei, however, in a move which showed his higher aims, did not fade into the background again. He positioned himself early in the bid for the support of AB!, particularly in the second year of the Lernei administration. He began to push further in favor of social programs, an irregular position of the party, while also continuing with the party's integration of cultural values and, as a foreigner himself, the deregulation of certain documentation methods in the country. Pictured as forward-thinking and prudent, the former Mavar officer found himself in the hotseat for the nomination again, and submitted a campaign to the AB! headquarters, also causing him to relocate to Deumibla. Garnei didn't cease with his talk after another electoral loss for Verticism, one which actually increased the potential of his own candidacy. And, among a shortened crowd looking to take the reins of the party, Garnei had an easier rise. Though, AB!, seemingly cautious in their selection without having to search for a replacement for the country's most popular politician, didn't select the businessman until the 16th of October. However, it is now clear that he's a clear player in the race, as would be expected of AB!.

The party's campaign for the presidency was instantaneously kickstarted, and Banhock social media quickly made #PoleToPole (English translation) a trending term, as there is now a definitive and apparently popular challenger to president Lernei. The most accurate BHE365 polls often come monthly, and as such indications will arrive within the next weeks. Though, now, the offices of the CGT, whom also found themselves in some hot water after it replaced their Junior Minister from the concurrent term in the campaign, must be interested in seeing how the new movement based on the distant, yet similar geographical locations will take advantage of the difficulties of the Lernei administration.
[/spoiler]
